items.abstract: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a leading cause of chronic low back pain (LBP), severely impairing patients' quality of life and imposing a substantial global socioeconomic burden. items.abstract: To clarify the efficacy and safety of Bufei Huoxue (BFHX) capsules for the treatment of pneumoconiosis. This multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial enrolled patients with pneum-oconiosis from five centers between June 2020 and June 2023. items.abstract: To evaluate and compare subepithelial connective tissue grafts (SCTG) and guided bone regeneration (GBR) for the treatment of small peri-implant buccal bone dehiscences over a 3-year follow-up, in terms of profilometric contour change, peri-implant parameters and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). items.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of self-operated home ultrasound for visual biofeedback training among nulliparous women, enabling visualization of fetal head descent and practice of second-stage pushing prior to labor. items.title: Classical popliteal sciatic block versus Crosswise Approach to Popliteal Sciatic (CAPS) block for below-knee surgery: a randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract: Ultrasound-guided popliteal sciatic nerve block is frequently used for below-knee surgery. The classical approach often requires lateral decubitus or prone positioning, which may be uncomfortable for patients with lower limb injuries. items.title: Quality of osteoporosis management guidelines produced in China: a systematic review.
items.abstract: This study employed the AGREE II and AGREE-REX instruments to assess the methodological rigor and recommendation quality of Chinese clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for osteoporosis care. A systematic search was conducted across CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang, VIP, Medlive, and the Chinese Medical Association website for CPGs published between January 2014 and December 2025. items.title: Breathing exercises as adjunct therapy in adult asthma: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Despite optimal pharmacological treatment, a substantial proportion of adult asthma patients remain symptomatic. Breathing exercises have emerged as a non-pharmacological adjunct specifically targeting dysfunctional breathing patterns (chronic hyperventilation, tachypnea, and aberrant ventilatory mechanics) that pharmacotherapy does not adequately address. items.title: Influencing factors of type 2 diabetes remission: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To identify factors influencing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remission and compare differences across intervention types and remission criteria. T2DM remission was defined as HbA1c < 6.5% (48 mmol/mol), measured at least 3 months after cessation of glucose-lowering pharmacotherapy. items.title: Gut mycobiome dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: The intestinal mycobiome is increasingly recognized as an important component of host-microbiota interactions in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet its contribution to intestinal immune dysregulation remains incompletely characterized. items.title: Heat Stroke Cooling Devices for Prehospital Use: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Heat stroke and heat exhaustion (HS/HE) are life-threatening conditions requiring immediate intervention. Cooling devices play a critical role in emergency and prehospital care, yet their effectiveness and field readiness are inconsistently reported. items.title: Artificial Intelligence-powered Advances in Phytomedicine: A Systematic Review on Plant-based Drug Discovery Software.
items.abstract: Herbal medicines contain complex phytochemicals that offer therapeutic potential, but their long-term adverse effects remain challenging to determine. items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in predicting late-onset intrauterine growth restriction in singleton pregnancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Late-onset intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is difficult to detect and is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning, for predicting late-onset IUGR in singleton pregnancies. items.title: Efficacy and safety of moxibustion therapy for bronchial asthma: a systematic review and network Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of different moxibustion therapies for treating asthma. Five databases were searched up to July 27, 2025, to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing moxibustion for bronchial asthma. items.title: Serum and salivary uric acid levels in oral submucous fibrosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate differences in serum uric acid (SeUA) and salivary uric acid (SaUA) levels between patients with oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) and healthy controls. items.title: The effect of diets enriched with high-oleic sources on anthropometric, inflammatory, and blood pressure outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: High-oleic diets (HODs) have been proposed to improve obesity-related and inflammatory outcomes, yet randomized evidence remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of HODs compared with low-oleic diets (LODs) on anthropometric, inflammatory, and blood pressure indices. items.title: Effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices and oxidative-stress biomarkers in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and dose-response analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: Diabetes and metabolic syndrome are major public health challenges closely linked to oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired insulin signaling. Selenium, an essential trace element with antioxidant and immunomodulatory roles, has been proposed as an adjunctive strategy for metabolic regulation; however, evidence from randomized trials remains inconsistent. items.title: Effects of prune on bone health; a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials.
items.abstract: Earlier randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating the effects of prune on bone health provided inconsistent findings. This study aims to summarize the literature and elucidate the effect of prune on bone health. In February 2025, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for RCTs. items.abstract: Nonspecific cytotoxic cell receptor protein 1 (NCCRP1), which is expressed in normal squamous epithelium, has been reported as a prognostic marker for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and triple-negative breast cancer. items.title: Pretransplant plasma soluble PD-1 and recurrence after liver transplantation in ICI-treated hepatocellular carcinoma: an exploratory biomarker study.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are increasingly used as bridging or downstaging therapy before liver transplantation (LT) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but biomarkers of posttransplant recurrence in this setting are lacking. items.title: Atrial Fibrillation in Tribal and Non-tribal Populations: A Comparative Analysis From Eastern India.
items.abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasingly prevalent arrhythmia in India, where rheumatic heart disease and cardiometabolic etiologies coexist. items.title: Physiological reserve and early recovery across oncologic and non-oncologic abdominal surgery: a prospective multicenter interaction analysis.
items.abstract: Frailty and low handgrip strength are established markers of limited physiological reserve, but it is uncertain whether their prognostic meaning differs between oncologic and non-oncologic surgery. items.title: Enteropathy in inborn and acquired errors of immunity: histological patterns and clinical correlates.
items.abstract: Enteropathy is a significant and under-recognised complication of inborn errors of immunity (IEI), frequently misclassified as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) or coeliac disease due to overlapping and non-specific histopathological findings. items.title: Association of MAGEA4 expression with molecular and immune subtypes and clinical outcomes in recurrent bladder cancer.
items.abstract: This study assessed MAGEA4 expression in recurrent bladder cancer, examined its relationships with molecular and immune subtypes, and evaluated its association with treatment response and prognosis. items.abstract: Accurate risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) is needed after endoscopic resection of early-stage colorectal cancer (CRC). items.abstract: Edematous malnutrition, aka kwashiorkor, is a phenotype of severe malnutrition whose pathophysiology remains poorly understood. items.title: School-weariness is associated with enhanced emotional stroop interference and selective autonomic differences in junior middle school students.
items.abstract: School-weariness (SW) is a pattern of persistent negative affect toward learning and school, with cognitive devaluation of academic activities. SW is associated with reduced academic motivation, poorer academic functioning, and internalizing/somatic problems, but its cognitive-affective processes and autonomic correlates remain unclear. items.title: Prevalence of Factor V Leiden mutation in yemeni women with gestational diabetes mellitus and recurrent pregnancy loss: a case-control study.
items.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most common metabolic disorders during pregnancy and has been associated with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and other obstetric complications. The Factor V Leiden (FVL) is a common inherited thrombophilic mutation. However, data on the prevalence of the FVL mutation among Yemeni women with GDM and a history of RPL remain scarce. items.title: Data-driven identification of modifiable risk factors for colorectal cancer in Palestine using machine learning methods.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a growing public health concern in Palestine, yet limited evidence is available on locally relevant behavioral, dietary, socioeconomic, and contextual predictors. Machine learning (ML) may support prevention-oriented risk stratification by identifying complex predictive patterns among potentially modifiable factors. items.title: Dietary frequency, body satisfaction, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms among offspring of healthcare workers in China.
items.abstract: Dietary behaviors may be associated with body image and emotional health in young people, but evidence integrating these outcomes in Chinese populations remains limited. This study examined associations of dietary frequency with body satisfaction, anxiety symptoms, and depressive symptoms. This cross-sectional study included 584 offspring of healthcare workers aged 10-24 years in Zhejiang, China.

items.abstract: In German-speaking countries, where geriatric care faces a persistent nursing shortage, nursing students are expected to play a key role in addressing future workforce needs. items.abstract: This study examined the associations between infant crawling experience and crawling characteristics and fundamental movement skill (FMS) development in preschool children to characterize population-level associations and generate hypotheses for prospective research. items.title: Gratitude and happiness among university students: a cross-sectional study in teacher education.
items.abstract: This study examined the association between gratitude and happiness among education students at a public university in Tacna, Peru, including four dimensions of happiness: positive sense of life, life satisfaction, personal fulfillment, and joy of living. items.abstract: To explore potential categories of nutritional literacy among adolescents with chronic kidney disease and differences in dietary motivations across these categories. items.title: Recent Update in the Diagnosis of Eustachian Tube Dysfunction: A Comprehensive Review of the Eustachian Tube Function Test.
items.abstract: Eustachian tube dysfunction (ETD) is a prevalent otolaryngologic condition that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of various middle ear diseases; however, there is no universally accepted gold-standard test for its diagnosis. items.title: Australian Speech-Language Pathologists' perspectives on using cervical auscultation in the detection of aspiration in infants and children.
items.abstract: Cervical auscultation (CA), a technique based on listening to swallow and breath sounds, has high diagnostic accuracy in detecting aspiration risk in children. Despite this, most Australian Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs) do not routinely use CA in clinical practice. items.abstract: Establishing optimal sarcopenia cutoffs is essential, as L3 is not always included in CT imaging, and reference levels vary across populations. The absence of Southeast Asia-specific thresholds may lead to misclassification, highlighting the need for regionally appropriate diagnostic criteria. items.abstract: To develop a novel quantitative scale for Damp-Heat Impeding Syndrome (DHIS) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and to enhance diagnostic reliability through a combined consensus- and data-driven approach grounded in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) principles, thereby addressing the limitations of existing expert-consensus-based tools. items.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is a complex disease characterized by inflammation, cartilage degeneration, and tissue remodeling. Although many biomarkers have been investigated, the combined biological significance of systemic and local biomarkers is not fully understood. items.title: Coronary artery compression in percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation: a case series.
items.abstract: Catastrophic complications of coronary artery compression after percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) are uncommon in patients with a dysfunctional native right ventricular outflow tract after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rTOF). items.abstract: Background Surgical management of traumatic cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage traditionally requires extensive craniotomy. Here, we present a tailored supraorbital craniotomy using an endoscopic technique for complex skull base trauma. items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are associated with a wide spectrum of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), reflecting enhanced immune activation. items.abstract: Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection. Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. items.abstract: Light-chain proximal tubulopathy (LCPT) is a rare renal manifestation of monoclonal gammopathy that is exceptionally uncommon in Waldenström macroglobulinemia (WM).
